analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date, clarifies that performance-measurement sample_age_ms is measured from the newest observation (even when an older completed observation arrives later), and adds a paragraph saying the Swift producer applies the same age rule per workload bucket and current-posture series (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe). It states that the wire fields are unchanged, that EWMA and sample counts keep receipt order, and that snapshot time does not replace observation time. I examined the changed ranges (base lines 578, head 578 and 580-586) and the surrounding base text in units 4-6. These are documentation-only changes with no code, wire schema, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior changes. They relate to capacity and performance telemetry, which the surrounding text already marks as diagnostic/advisory. The nearby text says the telemetry carries no prompt content, token IDs or cache keys, and the new text does not alter that. The only integration question is whether the actual Swift producer in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift, which is not in the supplied evidence, matches the doc. A mismatch would affect only provider-reported capacity freshness. That is an adversarial-provider concern already covered by coordinator-side validation and freshness reconciliation (reconcileCapacitySamples), so no threat-model entries (T-041 and others) are invalidated. No security regression identified, and no threat-model update is needed.
